title: Process lesson: instrument-first debugging for porting work
description:
Lesson from swisseph-rs/30-34: three sessions were spent reasoning about C pipeline behavior from a reference doc when the right move was to instrument the C code and diff intermediate values against Rust. Add to CLAUDE.md or docs/golden-testing.md:

1. When a golden test fails for a multi-step pipeline, FIRST write a C program that dumps intermediate values at each stage. Add matching Rust dumps. Diff to find the divergence point. Don't reason about code behavior — measure it.

2. Consider adding intermediate-stage golden tests (e.g., 'after light-time before deflection') to narrow failures faster.

3. When the C ref doc is ambiguous (loop bounds, flag guards, global state reads), instrument the C code rather than reasoning harder about pseudocode.
execution_record: Added instrument-first debugging protocol to docs/golden-testing.md and C source exception to CLAUDE.md. Stored FP += lesson in sutra. The core insight: planning wasn't the bottleneck — the implementation structure was correct from the start. The 1.5M tokens were burned on hypothesis-driven debugging (reason about C behavior → try a fix → run tests → repeat) when the instrument-and-diff approach found all three root causes in one pass.
